title: Black pepper shortbread
subtitle: buttery Scottish shortbread with a gentle heat from coarsely ground black pepper
excerpt: Black pepper in shortbread sounds unusual but the heat from the pepper cuts through the richness of the butter without being identifiable as pepper in the finished biscuit. The result is a more interesting, savoury-edged shortbread that pairs well with cheese as well as standing alone. Use freshly ground black pepper: pre-ground has no fragrance.
sourceNotes: Black pepper shortbread, a contemporary British savoury-sweet biscuit variant. Method based on the classic Scottish shortbread tradition (documented in Scottish cookbooks from the eighteenth century) with pepper addition.

glossaryTerms.definition: The characteristic sandy, crumbling, almost floury texture of shortbread, achieved by using cold butter rubbed into a flour and sugar mixture and baking at a low temperature until just set.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 3 weeks.

content.text: method: cold butter rubbed into flour and sugar, pressed into a tin, and baked low and slow. The only addition is coarsely ground black pepper. Use a heaped half teaspoon of pepper for a noticeable but not sharp heat; reduce to a quarter teaspoon for something much more subtle.

items.prepNote: for extra crunch (or use more plain flour)

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Lightly grease a 20 cm square tin and line with baking parchment.

Rub the cold butter into the flour (and rice flour if using), caster sugar, salt, and black pepper until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Squeeze the mixture together to form a dough; it will be dry and crumbly at first but will come together with pressing.
Press the dough evenly into the prepared tin. Prick all over with a fork. Sprinkle with granulated sugar if using. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until very pale golden and fully set. Score into fingers while still warm. Leave to cool completely in the tin before removing and snapping along the scored lines.

attrs.problem: Shortbread too hard and dry rather than crumbly
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-baking; shortbread should be pale throughout, not golden-brown.
attrs.fix: Reduce the bake time by 3 to 5 minutes next time. A well-made shortbread should press into crumbs, not snap rigidly.

attrs.problem: Pepper flavour very sharp or unpleasant
attrs.avoid: Avoid pre-ground pepper; the flavour is often stale and the grind is too fine.
attrs.fix: Use a coarse grind of fresh pepper from a pepper mill. Reduce the amount to 0.25 tsp if you prefer only a hint.
